title: Submodule Workflows
description: Use submodules effectively in team environments and CI pipelines.

data.text: Submodules introduce complexity in team environments because each developer must initialize and update them. A consistent workflow prevents 'missing submodule' errors and ensures everyone works with the same dependency versions.

data.title: Submodule workflow for teams
items: **Clone**: git clone <repo> followed by git submodule update --init --recursive
**Pull**: git pull followed by git submodule update --init --recursive
**Update a submodule**: Enter the submodule, pull, commit the new pointer
**Push**: Push both the parent repository and any submodule changes
**CI**: Run git submodule update --init --recursive before building

data.title: Complete submodule workflow
data.code:
# Developer: clone and initialize
git clone https://github.com/example/project.git
cd project
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Developer: pull latest changes
git pull origin main
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Developer: update a submodule to a newer commit
cd external/lib
git pull origin main
cd ../..
git add external/lib
git commit -m "chore: update lib to v2.3"
git push origin main

# CI: ensure submodules are present
git submodule update --init --recursive
npm install
npm test

data.text: Cloning with submodules in one command
Use git clone --recursive to clone a repository and all its submodules in a single step. This is equivalent to git clone followed by git submodule update --init --recursive.

data.title: Clone with submodules recursively
data.code:
# Clone and initialize all submodules in one step
git clone --recursive https://github.com/example/project.git
cd project

# Verify submodules are present
git submodule status

# If you forgot --recursive, initialize later
git submodule update --init --recursive

data.text: In CI environments, submodules are not automatically initialized. Add a step to your CI script to run git submodule update --init --recursive before building.

data.title: GitHub Actions workflow with submodules
data.code:
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive
      - run: npm install
      - run: npm test

data.text: When multiple developers update the same submodule to different commits, the parent repository can have a merge conflict on the submodule pointer. Resolve this by deciding which commit to use and committing the resolved pointer.

data.title: Resolve a submodule conflict
data.code:
# After git pull, you see:
# Auto-merging external/lib
# CONFLICT (submodule): Merge conflict in external/lib

# Resolve by entering the submodule and checking out the desired commit
cd external/lib
# Choose one of the two commits
git checkout <desired-commit-sha>
cd ../..

# Stage the resolved submodule pointer
git add external/lib
git commit -m "fix: resolve submodule conflict for lib"

data.title: Use SSH URLs for private submodules
data.text: If your submodule is in a private repository, use an SSH URL (git@github.com:...) instead of HTTPS. Configure CI secrets for SSH deployment keys so CI can access private submodules.
When you modify a submodule and want to share those changes, you must push from inside the submodule repository first, then push the updated pointer from the parent repository.

data.title: Push submodule and parent changes
data.code:
# Inside the submodule
external/lib$ git add .
external/lib$ git commit -m "feat: add new utility function"
external/lib$ git push origin main

# Back in the parent
external/lib$ cd ..
..$ git add external/lib
..$ git commit -m "chore: update lib submodule pointer"
..$ git push origin main

items.question: Can submodules track branches?
items.answer: By default, submodules record a specific commit SHA, not a branch. You can configure branch tracking with git config submodule.<name>.branch <branch-name>, but this is not the default behavior.

items.question: What if a submodule URL changes?
items.answer: Update the URL with git submodule set-url <path> <new-url>. This updates both the .gitmodules file and the .git/config entry.

items.question: How do I remove a submodule?
items.answer: Use git submodule deinit -f <path> followed by git rm -f <path>. Remove the entry from .gitmodules manually if needed.

items.question: Do submodules work in GitHub Codespaces?
items.answer: Yes. Codespaces automatically initializes submodules when you open a repository. Use the Codespaces settings to control submodule behavior.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use git clone --recursive to clone with submodules in one step
Always run git submodule update --init --recursive after pulling
Push submodule changes before pushing the parent pointer
Configure CI to initialize submodules before building
Use SSH URLs for private submodules and configure CI secrets
